questions.question: Compare and contrast the approaches of Ruth Benedict and Margaret Mead in studying the relationship between culture and personality.
questions.solution_html:
• Ruth Benedict emphasized how cultural patterns shape the collective personality of
  • societies, describing culture as a "personality writ large." She studied specific cultures, like
  • the Zuni and Dobu, to highlight their unique traits. Margaret Mead, however, focused on
  • how childhood socialization within different cultures influences personality development.
  • Her work, like the study of adolescence in Samoa, demonstrated the flexibility of human
  • behaviour across cultures. While Benedict emphasized the overarching cultural
  • framework, Mead highlighted the role of individual upbringing and social structures.
questions.final_answer: framework, Mead highlighted the role of individual upbringing and social structures
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) Regular Exam Sem 1, Nov 2024

questions.question: Discuss the psychological and social factors that contribute to the development of prejudice and stereotyping, END OF THE QUESTION PAPER ***
questions.solution_html:
• Psychological factors, such as cognitive biases like categorization and in-group
  • favouritism, lead to generalizations and prejudices. Fear of the unknown and personal
  • insecurities also contribute to stereotyping. Social factors include cultural norms and
  • values that perpetuate stereotypes through socialization. Media representations and
  • unequal power dynamics in society further reinforce these biases. Together, these factors
  • create and sustain prejudice in individual and group interactions.
  • (1 × 10 = 10)
